key_insight: Hierarchical randomized neural networks combine SVD-guided initialization, deflated optimization, and multilevel refinement to efficiently find multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help computational engineers explore multiple nonlinear PDE solutions without requiring prior knowledge of their structure.
method: Use a characteristic matrix and its SVD to identify weakly varying search directions and generate initial candidates.
Apply good deflated Gauss–Newton optimization with exponential deflation to seek distinct solutions.
Use hierarchical network levels to accelerate computation and improve accuracy.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests report relative errors reaching 10⁻¹⁶, computational cost below one-tenth of the comparison cost in the best case, and preservation of solution symmetries.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish exhaustive solution discovery; accuracy and cost gains may depend on the problem, network size, and sampling.
paper_title: Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
